title: Messages Inbox
intro: Ten messages landed. Which are traps of the heart or the wallet?
Swipe left if it is a scam, right if it is safe. Or tap the buttons.
Careful: some are honest. Do not cry wolf.

cards.text: I feel like I have known you forever. Let us move to a private app.
cards.why: Fast love and a move to a private app is the script.

cards.text: Dinner at 7 on Sunday? Dad is making soup.
Please send 600 USDT for my papers.
cards.why: Money for papers from a love far away is a scam.

cards.text: Your appointment is tomorrow at 3. Reply C to confirm.
cards.why: A normal reminder with no link or money.

cards.text: My camera is broken again. Send 800 USDT for a trade.
cards.why: Never on camera plus money is the scam.

cards.text: Your book is due in 3 days. Renew on the library site you use.
cards.why: A normal notice pointing to a site you already use.

cards.text: Look at my profits! Download my app to join.
cards.why: A private trading app from a new friend is a trap.

cards.text: Are you at your desk? Send 2,000 USDT now. Keep it quiet.
cards.why: A boss from a new number asking for crypto is an impersonator.

cards.text: Coffee on Saturday? Same café as last time.
cards.why: A normal plan from a known friend.

cards.text: We can recover your lost funds for a 10% fee.
cards.why: Recovery services that charge up front are scams.

golden_rule: If someone you have never met asks for money, crypto or secrecy, it is a scam, however sweet.

options.text: A new match asking to move to a private app
A friend suggesting coffee at the usual café
A boss from a new number asking for USDT
A recovery desk asking for a fee

quick_check.explain: It is a known friend with no money and no pressure.
